content: Non-tubal ectopic pregnancy refers to the implantation of an embryo in locations outside the uterine cavity or fallopian tubes. These locations can include a cesarean scar, the uterine cornua, the ovary, the cervix, or the abdominal cavity. There has been a notable increase in the incidence of these rare conditions, particularly cesarean scar pregnancies (CSP). The objective of this research was to assess the clinical effectiveness and safety of surgical interventions, medical treatments, and expectant management for non-tubal ectopic pregnancies, with a focus on fertility outcomes and complications. To gather data, a comprehensive search was conducted across multiple databases, including the Cochrane Gynaecology and Fertility Group Specialised Register of Controlled Trials, CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, ClinicalTrials.gov, the World Health Organization search portal, and nine additional databases. The search was completed on December 12, 2019. Reference lists of retrieved articles were also reviewed, and experts in the field were contacted to obtain further information. The study included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) in any language that evaluated the effects and safety of surgical, medical, and expectant management approaches for non-tubal ectopic pregnancies. Standard Cochrane methodological procedures were employed for data collection and analysis. The primary outcomes assessed were treatment success and complications. Five RCTs involving 303 women were included in the analysis, all of which focused on cesarean scar pregnancies. Two trials compared uterine arterial embolization (UAE) or uterine arterial chemoembolization (UACE) combined with methotrexate (MTX) versus systemic MTX followed by dilation and suction curettage. One trial compared UACE combined with MTX versus ultrasonography-guided local MTX injection. Two trials compared suction curettage performed under hysteroscopy versus suction curettage performed under ultrasonography, both following UAE or UACE. The quality of evidence ranged from moderate to very low, with limitations including small sample sizes, wide confidence intervals, multiple comparisons with few trials, and insufficient data to assess heterogeneity. Comparison of UAE/UACE versus systemic MTX prior to suction curettage: Two studies evaluated this comparison. One compared UAE with systemic MTX, and the other compared UACE combined with MTX versus systemic MTX, both followed by suction curettage. It is uncertain whether UAE or UACE improved treatment success rates after the initial intervention. For UAE, the risk ratio (RR) was 1.00 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.90 to 1.12; 1 RCT, 72 women; low-quality evidence). For UACE, the RR was 0.87 (95% CI 0.54 to 1.38; 1 RCT, 28 women; low-quality evidence). It is uncertain whether UAE or UACE reduced complication rates. For UAE, the RR was 0.47 (95% CI 0.13 to 1.75; 1 RCT, 72 women; low-quality evidence). For UACE, the RR was 0.62 (95% CI 0.26 to 1.48; 1 RCT, 28 women; low-quality evidence). It is uncertain whether UAE or UACE reduced adverse effects. For UAE, the RR was 1.58 (95% CI 0.41 to 6.11; 1 RCT, 72 women; low-quality evidence). For UACE, the RR was 1.16 (95% CI 0.32 to 4.24; 1 RCT, 28 women; low-quality evidence). The types of adverse events (e.g., fever versus vomiting) were not clearly comparable. Blood loss was lower in the UAE and UACE groups compared to the systemic MTX groups. For UAE, the mean difference (MD) was –378.70 mL (95% CI –401.43 to –355.97; 1 RCT, 72 women; moderate-quality evidence). For UACE, the MD was –879.00 mL (95% CI –1135.23 to –622.77; 1 RCT, 28 women; moderate-quality evidence). Data on the time to normalize β-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) levels were not available. Comparison of UACE plus MTX versus ultrasonography-guided local MTX injection: It is uncertain whether UACE improved treatment success rates after the initial intervention. The RR was 0.95 (95% CI 0.56 to 1.60; 1 RCT, 45 women; very low-quality evidence). The study reported an equal number of failed treatments in both groups. The RR was 0.88 (95% CI 0.40 to 1.92; 1 RCT, 45 women). It is uncertain whether UACE shortened the time to normalize β-hCG levels. The MD was 1.50 days (95% CI –3.16 to 6.16; 1 RCT, 45 women; very low-quality evidence). Data on complications were not available. Comparison of suction curettage under hysteroscopy versus under ultrasonography after UAE/UACE: Two studies evaluated this comparison. One compared suction curettage under hysteroscopy versus under ultrasonography after UAE, and the other compared these interventions after UACE. It is uncertain whether suction curettage under hysteroscopy improved treatment success rates after the initial intervention. For UAE, the RR was 0.91 (95% CI 0.81 to 1.03; 1 RCT, 66 women; very low-quality evidence). For UACE, the RR was 1.02 (95% CI 0.96 to 1.09; 1 RCT, 92 women; low-quality evidence). It is uncertain whether suction curettage under hysteroscopy reduced complication rates. For UAE, the RR was 4.00 (95% CI 0.47 to 33.91; 1 RCT, 66 women; very low-quality evidence). For UACE, the RR was 0.18 (95% CI 0.01 to 3.72; 1 RCT, 92 women; low-quality evidence). It is uncertain whether suction curettage under hysteroscopy reduced adverse effects. For UAE, the RR was 3.09 (95% CI 0.12 to 78.70; 1 RCT, 66 women; very low-quality evidence). For UACE, the data were not estimable (1 RCT, 92 women; very low-quality evidence). It is uncertain whether suction curettage under hysteroscopy shortened the time to normalize β-hCG levels. For UAE, the MD was 4.03 days (95% CI –1.79 to 9.85; 1 RCT, 66 women; very low-quality evidence). For UACE, the MD was 0.84 days (95% CI –1.90 to 3.58; 1 RCT, 92 women; low-quality evidence). Non-tubal ectopic pregnancies other than CSP: No studies were identified that addressed non-tubal ectopic pregnancies in locations other than cesarean scars. Conclusions: For cesarean scar pregnancies, it remains uncertain whether UAE or UACE combined with systemic MTX before suction curettage offers better success rates, fewer complications, or fewer adverse events compared to systemic MTX alone (low-quality evidence). However, blood loss was lower when suction curettage was performed after UAE or UACE compared to systemic MTX (moderate-quality evidence). It is uncertain whether suction curettage under hysteroscopy is superior to suction curettage under ultrasonography in terms of treatment success, complications, adverse effects, or time to normalize β-hCG levels (very low-quality evidence). No RCTs were identified for non-tubal ectopic pregnancies in locations other than cesarean scars, and it is unlikely that such trials will be conducted.
